title_tag: 给孩子留100万，还是花100万培养他？哪一种回报更高？—— 英国《经济学人》外刊讲解第1188天
h1: 给孩子留100万，还是花100万培养他？哪一种回报更高？
category: 英国《经济学人》外刊讲解 第1188天
nav_hint: Investing for babies involves knotty trade-offs

headline.en_html: Investing for babies involves knotty trade-offs — Should new parents favour financial capital, human capital or something else?
headline.zh: 给婴儿做投资，是一道难解的取舍题——新手父母该押注金融资本、人力资本，还是别的什么？

notes.en: knotty means complicated and difficult to solve, like a tangle that cannot be pulled apart
notes.ctx: 标题先定调：给婴儿做投资不是一道算数题，而是一团解不开的结。
notes.ex1: The merger raised a knotty question about which management team would survive. 这桩合并抛出了一个棘手的问题：两套管理层究竟留谁。
notes.ex2: Regulators are still untangling the knotty issue of who owns the training data. 监管机构仍在梳理“训练数据归谁所有”这个盘根错节的难题。

notes.en: a trade-off means a situation in which you accept less of one thing in order to get more of another
notes.ctx: 副标题把选择摊开：金融资本、人力资本，还是别的什么？父母手里的钱只有一份。
notes.ex1: Every chip designer faces a trade-off between raw speed and battery life. 每一个芯片设计者都要在纯性能和续航之间做取舍。
notes.ex2: There is an unavoidable trade-off between keeping prices low and paying workers more. 压低价格和给工人加薪之间，存在无法回避的取舍。

notes.en: favour means to prefer or choose one option over the others available
notes.ctx: 副标题的动词：不是“给”，而是“押注在哪一边”。
notes.ex1: Younger investors increasingly favour index funds over actively managed products. 年轻投资者越来越倾向于指数基金，而不是主动管理型产品。
notes.ex2: The latest evidence favours the simpler explanation. 最新的证据更支持那个比较简单的解释。

notes.en: human capital means the knowledge, skills and health that a person possesses and that can generate future income
notes.ctx: 与“金融资本”对举：花在孩子健康、教育和技能上的那部分投入。
notes.ex1: Singapore’s growth story is largely a story of relentless human-capital investment. 新加坡的增长故事，很大程度上就是一部持续投资人力资本的历史。
notes.ex2: When a factory closes, the loss of human capital often outlasts the loss of jobs. 工厂关门时，人力资本的流失往往比岗位的消失影响更久。

paragraphs.en_html: Patience, consistency and <mark class="voc">frugality</mark> are fine habits for an investor. They are not, however, common <mark class="voc">virtues</mark> among newborn babies. The little <mark class="voc">bundles of joy</mark> are <mark class="voc">impulsive</mark> short-term thinkers. They are also some of nature’s biggest <mark class="voc">freeloaders</mark>, <mark class="voc">living entirely beyond their means</mark>.
paragraphs.zh: 耐心、自律、节俭，是投资者身上难得的好习惯。可惜啊，这些美德在新生儿身上基本见不着。这些被襁褓裹着的“小开心果”，是一群冲动的短期主义者。他们还是大自然里头号的白吃白喝党——花的钱，一分不是自己挣的。

notes.en: frugality means the habit of being careful with money and avoiding waste
notes.ctx: 作者列出的投资者三大美德之一，专门用来和婴儿的挥霍形成反差。
notes.ex1: The founder’s frugality became company legend: he flew economy until the IPO. 这位创始人的节俭成了公司传奇——上市之前他一直坐经济舱。
notes.ex2: Years of frugality allowed the couple to retire a decade early. 多年省吃俭用，让这对夫妻提前十年退休。

notes.en: virtue means a good quality or moral strength in a person’s character
notes.ctx: 指耐心、稳定、节俭这三样；作者说它们在新生儿身上基本见不着。
notes.ex1: She got the job by virtue of her years on the trading floor. 她能拿到这份工作，靠的是在交易大厅摸爬滚打的那些年。
notes.ex2: The design has the virtue of being almost impossible to break. 这个设计有一个好处：几乎弄不坏。

notes.en: a bundle of joy means a newborn baby, seen as a source of happiness for the family
notes.ctx: 用最甜腻的说法称呼婴儿，紧接着就调侃他们不会理财，先捧后摔。
notes.ex1: The couple posted a photo of their new bundle of joy at 3am. 这对夫妻凌晨三点晒出了他们刚出生的小宝贝的照片。
notes.ex2: Six weeks in, the bundle of joy was mostly a bundle of laundry. 孩子出生六周后，这个“开心小包裹”主要变成了一堆要洗的衣服。

notes.en: impulsive means acting suddenly on feeling, without stopping to think about the consequences
notes.ctx: 婴儿想哭就哭、想要就要，和投资者需要的耐心完全相反。
notes.ex1: Retailers put chocolate by the till precisely to trigger impulse buying. 零售商把巧克力摆在收银台旁边，就是为了诱发冲动消费。
notes.ex2: His impulsive resignation cost him a bonus worth six months’ pay. 他一冲动辞了职，代价是半年工资的奖金。

notes.en: a freeloader means someone who takes food, money or help from others without giving anything back
notes.zh: 白吃白喝的人，爱占便宜的人
notes.ctx: 婴儿吃穿住全靠父母、一分钱不挣，被作者封为“大自然里最大的白嫖党”。
notes.ex1: He spent his twenties freeloading off a succession of patient friends. 他二十多岁那几年，一直在一群好脾气的朋友家白吃白住。
notes.ex2: The subscription model finally made it hard for freeloaders to use the service. 订阅制终于让白嫖的人没那么容易用上这项服务了。

notes.en: to live beyond one’s means is to spend more money than you earn or can afford
notes.zh: 入不敷出，花得比挣得多
notes.ctx: 婴儿收入为零，他花的每一分钱都在财力之外，entirely 把这个玩笑钉死。
notes.ex1: Half the households in the survey admitted living beyond their means last year. 调查中有一半家庭承认，去年是入不敷出的。
notes.ex2: His advice was unglamorous: live within your means and start early. 他的建议一点也不花哨——量入为出，尽早开始。

paragraphs.en_html: <mark class="voc">All the same</mark>, for new parents with <mark class="voc">a soft spot for</mark> the magic of <mark class="voc">compounding</mark>, like your columnist, a baby <mark class="voc">presents</mark> a <mark class="voc">tantalising</mark> investment opportunity. Many decades of life and potential returns <mark class="voc">stretch out</mark> into the future: $1,000 invested today with a real annual return of 5.2% (the average for global stocks over the past 125 years) would be worth $58,000 by the time the child is 80.
paragraphs.zh: 话说回来，对于那些对复利魔力毫无抵抗力的新手父母——比如本栏作者我——一个婴儿，简直就是一个馋得人抓心挠肝的投资机会。几十年的人生和潜在回报，就这么一路向未来铺展开去：今天投进1000美元，按5.2%的实际年化回报算（这是过去125年全球股市的平均水平），等孩子80岁那年，这笔钱将值58000美元。

notes.en: all the same means in spite of what has just been said; nevertheless
notes.ctx: 先承认婴儿是白嫖党，再借这个短语转向“他仍然是个绝佳投资标的”。
notes.ex1: The deal looks risky; all the same, the board approved it unanimously. 这桩交易看着很冒险，尽管如此，董事会还是一致通过了。
notes.ex2: Cash or card — it’s all the same to me. 现金还是刷卡，对我来说都一样。

notes.en: to have a soft spot for something means to feel a special, slightly irrational fondness for it
notes.zh: 对……特别偏爱，毫无抵抗力
notes.ctx: 作者自嘲：就是那种“一听复利就心动”的新手爸爸。
notes.ex1: The chairman has a soft spot for loss-making bookshops, which explains the acquisition. 董事长对亏损的书店有种偏爱，这笔收购就说得通了。
notes.ex2: I have a soft spot for companies that still answer the phone. 我对那些还肯接电话的公司有好感。

notes.en: compounding means the process in which investment returns are reinvested so that they themselves earn returns
notes.ctx: 就是让 1000 美元在 80 年里变成 58000 美元的那股力量，第 9 段还会再回扣一次。
notes.ex1: Over thirty years, compounding does more work than stock-picking ever will. 三十年下来，复利干的活儿比选股多得多。
notes.ex2: Delaying the recall compounded an already serious reputational problem. 推迟召回，让本已严重的声誉问题雪上加霜。

notes.en: present means to offer, provide or constitute something, such as an opportunity or a difficulty
notes.ctx: 一个婴儿“构成了”一个诱人的投资机会——不是 give，而是端到眼前。
notes.ex1: The slump in freight rates presents an opportunity for buyers with cash. 运价暴跌，给手握现金的买家带来了机会。
notes.ex2: Scaling the pilot nationwide presents a logistical challenge of a different order. 把试点推向全国，带来的是另一个量级的物流挑战。

notes.en: tantalising means attractive and desirable but kept just out of reach
notes.zh: 诱人却够不着的，让人心痒的
notes.ctx: 那笔要到孩子 80 岁才兑现的收益，父母算得出，却大概率看不到。
notes.ex1: The trailer offered a tantalising glimpse of the new engine and nothing else. 预告片只给了新引擎惊鸿一瞥，别的什么也没透露。
notes.ex2: For years a cure remained tantalisingly close but never quite arrived. 多年来，治愈方案一直近在咫尺，却始终没有真正到来。

notes.en: stretch out means to extend over a long distance or a long period of time
notes.ctx: 婴儿面前那几十年人生和潜在收益，像一条望不到头的路向未来铺开。
notes.ex1: The salt flats stretched out before us for forty unbroken kilometres. 盐滩在我们面前一口气铺开了四十公里。
notes.ex2: Repayment stretches out over twenty-five years, which is the whole point. 还款期一直拖到二十五年——这正是关键所在。

paragraphs.en_html: Yet these <mark class="voc">juicy</mark> financial returns must be considered <mark class="voc">alongside</mark> another sort of investment: in the children themselves. Spending on a child’s health, education and skills can <mark class="voc">yield</mark> even higher returns (<mark class="voc">on top of</mark> helping them lead a <mark class="voc">fulfilling</mark> life). So how should a new parent think about their <mark class="voc">budding</mark> little <mark class="voc">portfolio</mark>?
paragraphs.zh: 不过，这些肥美的金融回报，还得跟另一种投资摆在一起掂量——那就是投到孩子本身。花在孩子健康、教育和技能上的钱，回报率可能还要更高（顺带还能让他这辈子过得充实一点）。那么问题来了：新手爸妈该怎么看待自己手上这个刚刚发芽的小小“投资组合”呢？

notes.en: juicy means full of juice; informally, rich, rewarding or full of interesting detail
notes.ctx: 指前两段算出来的那笔“肥美”的金融回报。
notes.ex1: The contract came with a juicy margin that rivals could not match. 这份合同的利润率高得对手跟不上。
notes.ex2: She had some genuinely juicy gossip about the board reshuffle. 关于董事会改组，她手里有些真正有料的八卦。

notes.en: alongside means next to and at the same time as something else, often for comparison
notes.ctx: 金融回报必须和“投资孩子本身”这条路摆在一起掂量，不能只看一边。
notes.ex1: The new model will sit alongside the existing range rather than replace it. 新款将与现有产品线并存，而不是取代它。
notes.ex2: These costs must be read alongside the savings they generate. 这些成本必须和它们带来的节省放在一起看。

notes.en: yield means to produce or generate a profit, result or crop; as a noun, the rate of return on an investment
notes.ctx: 花在孩子健康、教育和技能上的钱“能产出更高的回报”——熟词僻义，本义是“交出”。
notes.ex1: The portfolio yielded just under 6% last year, net of fees. 这个组合去年扣费后的收益略低于6%。
notes.ex2: Falling bond yields pushed investors back towards equities. 债券收益率下行，把投资者又推回了股票。

notes.en: on top of means in addition to something that already exists
notes.ctx: 教育投资不只回报更高，还额外帮孩子过上充实人生——作者故意把这层放进括号。
notes.ex1: On top of the tariff, importers now face a new licensing fee. 除了关税，进口商现在还要交一笔新的牌照费。
notes.ex2: On top of everything else, the server went down during the launch. 偏偏在发布的时候，服务器还宕机了。

notes.en: fulfilling means making you feel satisfied and that what you do has meaning
notes.ctx: 教育投资那层“非经济”回报：让孩子这辈子过得有意义，而不只是赚得多。
notes.ex1: She left banking for a lower-paid but far more fulfilling job in teaching. 她离开了银行业，去做一份工资低得多、却充实得多的教师工作。
notes.ex2: Most people want work that is fulfilling, not merely tolerable. 大多数人想要的是有成就感的工作，而不只是能忍受的工作。

notes.en: budding means beginning to grow or develop and showing promise
notes.ctx: 形容婴儿这个“小小投资组合”：组合刚起步，生命也刚冒头，一语双关。
notes.ex1: The programme is designed for budding founders who have yet to raise a round. 这个项目是为还没融过资的初创者设计的。
notes.ex2: Management nipped the rumour in the bud with a blunt internal memo. 管理层用一份措辞直白的内部通报，把谣言扼杀在了萌芽里。

notes.en: a portfolio means the whole collection of investments held by a person or institution
notes.ctx: 作者把自己怀里的婴儿称作“刚发芽的小小投资组合”。
notes.ex1: A diversified portfolio would have ridden out the shock with far less damage. 一个分散的投资组合，本可以把这次冲击的损失降到低得多的水平。
notes.ex2: Her portfolio got her the interview; the interview got her the job. 她的作品集让她拿到了面试，面试让她拿到了工作。

paragraphs.en_html: Potential financial investments are <mark class="voc">manifold</mark>. Many countries offer <mark class="voc">tax-advantaged</mark> ways for parents to save for their children. American <mark class="voc">tykes</mark> are now <mark class="voc">eligible</mark> for Trump accounts, which start with a $1,000 <mark class="voc">freebie</mark> from the federal government that can be put into mutual funds or index trackers until the child turns 18, while taxes are <mark class="voc">deferred</mark>. Earlier options include the even more tax-friendly 529 accounts, but these may be used <mark class="voc">solely</mark> for <mark class="voc">specified</mark> educational purposes. In Britain, the Junior Individual Savings Account, into which up to £9,000 ($11,900) a year can be invested, is tax-friendlier still.
paragraphs.zh: 可选的金融工具五花八门。不少国家都给父母准备了带税收优惠的攒钱通道。美国的小娃娃现在够资格开“特朗普账户”了——开户联邦政府就白送1000美元，这笔钱可以投进共同基金或指数基金，一直放到孩子满18岁，期间税款递延。更早就有的选项里，还有税收优惠更大的529账户，但这笔钱只能花在规定好的教育用途上。而在英国，少年个人储蓄账户（Junior ISA）每年最多可以投进9000英镑（约合11900美元），税上还要更划算。

notes.en: manifold means many and of several different kinds
notes.zh: 多种多样的，名目繁多的
notes.ctx: 可供父母选择的金融投资工具五花八门。
notes.ex1: The benefits of early screening are manifold and well documented. 早期筛查的好处多种多样，而且有充分记录。
notes.ex2: Her reasons for leaving were manifold, and money was the least of them. 她离职的理由有一大堆，钱是最次要的那个。

notes.en: tax-advantaged describes an account or investment that receives favourable treatment under tax law
notes.ctx: 指各国为父母准备的儿童储蓄账户：特朗普账户、529、Junior ISA。
notes.ex1: Most of her retirement savings sit in tax-advantaged accounts she cannot touch until 60. 她的退休储蓄大多放在60岁前动不了的免税账户里。
notes.ex2: The budget quietly narrowed several long-standing tax breaks for landlords. 这份预算案悄悄收窄了几项针对房东的长期税收优惠。

notes.en: a tyke means a small child, especially a cheeky or mischievous one
notes.ctx: 指美国的新生儿——一篇正经财经文章里，故意用个俏皮词。
notes.ex1: The little tyke had hidden the car keys in the dog’s bed. 这小鬼头把车钥匙藏在了狗窝里。
notes.ex2: Two tykes in matching raincoats were stamping in every puddle on the street. 两个穿着同款雨衣的小家伙，把街上每个水坑都踩了一遍。

notes.en: eligible means having the right qualifications or meeting the conditions to do or receive something
notes.ctx: 美国新生儿现在够资格开设特朗普账户。
notes.ex1: Only households earning under the threshold are eligible for the rebate. 只有收入低于这条线的家庭才有资格拿到这笔返款。
notes.ex2: He became, in the language of old novels, a highly eligible bachelor. 用老派小说的说法，他成了一位极其抢手的黄金单身汉。

notes.en: a freebie means something you are given without having to pay for it
notes.ctx: 联邦政府往特朗普账户里白送的那 1000 美元。
notes.ex1: The stand was mobbed the moment they started handing out freebies. 他们一开始发赠品，展台立刻就被围住了。
notes.ex2: Treat the first month as a freebie; the real cost starts in month two. 把第一个月当成白送的，真正的成本从第二个月才开始。

notes.en: defer means to postpone something until a later time
notes.ctx: 账户里的收益现在不交税、以后再交，期间继续滚复利。
notes.ex1: The company deferred the dividend to preserve cash through the downturn. 公司推迟了分红，以便在低迷期保住现金。
notes.ex2: On technical questions, the board tends to defer to its chief engineer. 碰到技术问题，董事会一般听总工程师的。

notes.en: solely means only, and not involving anything or anyone else
notes.ctx: 529 账户的钱只能花在规定好的教育用途上，不得挪作他用。
notes.ex1: The fund may be used solely for capital projects, not salaries. 这笔资金只能用于基建项目，不能发工资。
notes.ex2: She is solely responsible for everything that leaves this building. 从这栋楼里发出去的一切，都由她一个人负责。

notes.en: specified means clearly and explicitly stated in advance
notes.ctx: 指 529 账户白纸黑字写明的那些教育开支项目。
notes.ex1: Delivery must take place within the specified window or the order lapses. 必须在规定的时间窗口内交货，否则订单作废。
notes.ex2: Unless otherwise specified, all figures are in constant 2020 dollars. 除另有说明外，所有数字均以2020年不变美元计。

paragraphs.en_html: Investing for babies is a joy even without the tax <mark class="voc">perks</mark>. Long <mark class="voc">horizons</mark> <mark class="voc">smooth out</mark> <mark class="voc">volatility</mark>, allowing for more risk. Ian Ayres and Barry Nalebuff, two economists, propose that young workers should borrow to buy stocks, since the long-term returns to <mark class="voc">equities</mark> are (hopefully) higher than the interest on borrowing. If the logic is true for <mark class="voc">20-somethings</mark>, it is truer still for infants with a horizon a couple of decades longer.
paragraphs.zh: 就算没有那些税收优惠，给婴儿做投资本身也是件乐事。时间一拉长，波动就被熨平了，于是你反倒敢多担一点风险。经济学家伊恩·艾尔斯和巴里·奈尔伯夫就主张，年轻的上班族应该借钱买股票——理由是，股票的长期回报（但愿）会高过借钱的利息。要是这套逻辑对二十来岁的人站得住，那对投资期限还要再长上二三十年的婴儿来说，就更站得住了。

notes.en: a perk means an extra benefit that comes with a job or a situation, beyond the main reward
notes.ctx: 指那些儿童账户的税收优惠——作者说就算没有，给婴儿投资本身也值得做。
notes.ex1: Free childcare is the one perk that actually keeps staff from leaving. 免费托儿是唯一真正能留住员工的福利。
notes.ex2: A double espresso usually perks him up enough to finish the model. 一杯双份浓缩通常能让他提起精神把模型做完。

notes.en: a horizon is the line where land meets sky; in finance, the length of time over which an investment is held
notes.ctx: 婴儿拥有比成年人长几十年的投资期限，这是全文最核心的资源。
notes.ex1: With a thirty-year horizon, a bad quarter is simply noise. 在三十年的投资期限里，一个糟糕的季度不过是噪音。
notes.ex2: A merger of this size has been on the horizon for months. 这种量级的合并，几个月前就已经看得见苗头了。

notes.en: smooth out means to remove irregularities so that something becomes even and steady
notes.ctx: 足够长的期限会把短期剧烈波动熨平，于是你反倒敢多担风险。
notes.ex1: Hedging contracts smooth out the swings in fuel costs across the year. 对冲合约把全年燃料成本的起伏抹平了。
notes.ex2: A long chat over dinner smoothed out most of the differences. 一顿饭聊下来，大部分分歧都化解了。

notes.en: volatility means the tendency of a price or situation to change rapidly and unpredictably
notes.ctx: 指被长期限熨平的那种短期剧烈起伏。
notes.ex1: Traders made more money from the volatility than from the direction. 交易员从波动里赚的钱，比从方向里赚的还多。
notes.ex2: Lithium prices have been volatile enough to bankrupt two suppliers. 锂价波动之大，已经让两家供应商破了产。

notes.en: equity means ownership shares in a company; also the value of an asset after debts against it are deducted
notes.ctx: 指两位经济学家所说“长期回报高于借款利息”的那类资产。
notes.ex1: The fund shifted a third of its bond holdings into equities last quarter. 该基金上季度把三分之一的债券仓位换成了股票。
notes.ex2: Rising prices quietly handed homeowners a great deal of extra home equity. 房价上涨，悄悄给房主增加了大量的房屋净值。

notes.en: a 20-something means a person whose age is between twenty and twenty-nine
notes.ctx: Ayres 与 Nalebuff 建议“借钱买股票”的目标人群，作者接着把逻辑推到比他们还小二十年的婴儿身上。
notes.ex1: Most of the app’s users are 20-somethings who have never owned a chequebook. 这款应用的用户大多是二十几岁、从没用过支票本的人。
notes.ex2: The company is run almost entirely by thirty-somethings. 这家公司几乎完全由三十多岁的人在经营。

paragraphs.en_html: Some parents fear that creating a large <mark class="voc">trust fund</mark> will turn their <mark class="voc">offspring</mark> into <mark class="voc">layabouts</mark>. Andrew Carnegie, a 19th-century American steel <mark class="voc">magnate</mark>, <mark class="voc">gave away</mark> most of his wealth out of fear that it would <mark class="voc">dull</mark> the <mark class="voc">work ethic</mark> of his descendants. A more recent study of Norwegian inheritances between 2000 and 2004 found that those <mark class="voc">bequeathed</mark> NKr300,000 (some $40,000 at the time) or more reduced their working hours by 7-10% in the six years that followed.
paragraphs.zh: 也有父母担心，给孩子留一大笔信托基金，会把后代养成游手好闲的废人。19世纪的美国钢铁大王安德鲁·卡内基，就是出于这份担忧——怕钱会磨钝子孙的奋斗心——把大半身家都捐了出去。一项更近的研究，考察了挪威2000至2004年间的遗产继承，结果发现：凡是继承到30万挪威克朗（当时约合4万美元）以上的人，在随后的六年里，工作时长减少了7%到10%。

notes.en: a trust fund means money or property held and managed by trustees on behalf of a beneficiary, under rules set by the person who created it
notes.ctx: 父母担心会把孩子养成废人的那笔大额财产安排；第 10 段又说“哪怕只是一笔不大的信托”也可能养懒。
notes.ex1: The estate was placed in a trust fund that pays out only after the heirs turn thirty. 这笔遗产被放进一个信托，继承人满三十岁才开始领取。
notes.ex2: “Trust-fund baby” is rarely meant as a compliment. “信托基金宝宝”这个说法，基本不是在夸人。

notes.en: offspring means a person’s children, or the young of an animal
notes.ctx: 指父母担心会被巨额信托养成 layabout 的那些孩子。
notes.ex1: The pair raise two offspring a season and abandon the nest by August. 这对鸟一季养育两只幼崽，八月前就弃巢。
notes.ex2: The policy is the offspring of a compromise nobody much liked. 这项政策是一个谁都不太满意的妥协的产物。

notes.en: a layabout means a lazy person who avoids work and does nothing useful
notes.ctx: 父母最怕孩子因为继承财产变成的那种人，与第 1 段的 freeloader 遥相呼应。
notes.ex1: He was written off as a layabout until, at thirty-one, he founded the company. 他一直被当成游手好闲的废人，直到三十一岁创办了这家公司。
notes.ex2: The scheme was attacked for rewarding layabouts and punishing savers. 这个方案被批评为奖励懒人、惩罚储蓄者。

notes.en: a magnate means a rich and powerful person who dominates a particular industry
notes.ctx: 指 19 世纪的美国钢铁大王安德鲁·卡内基。
notes.ex1: A shipping magnate bought the yard in 1998 and never once visited it. 一位航运大亨1998年买下了这家船厂，之后一次都没去过。
notes.ex2: The media magnate’s retirement triggered a three-way succession fight. 这位传媒大亨退休，引发了三方争夺继承权的局面。

notes.en: give away means to hand something over for nothing, or to reveal something unintentionally
notes.ctx: 卡内基把大半身家捐了出去，为的是不让财富磨钝后代。
notes.ex1: He gave away almost the entire fortune before his seventieth birthday. 他在七十岁生日之前，几乎把全部财产都捐了出去。
notes.ex2: Her face was a dead giveaway the moment the number was read out. 数字一念出来，她的表情就全露馅了。

notes.pos: v.（形容词义之外的动词用法）
notes.en: dull means to make something less sharp, less strong or less keen
notes.ctx: 卡内基怕财富一点点磨掉子孙的奋斗劲儿——是渐进磨损，不是一次性摧毁。
notes.ex1: Two decades of easy profits dulled the firm’s appetite for risk. 二十年的轻松利润，磨掉了这家公司冒险的胃口。
notes.ex2: Nothing dulls a good idea faster than three rounds of committee review. 没有什么比三轮委员会评审更能磨掉一个好点子。

notes.en: work ethic means the belief that hard work is intrinsically valuable, and the habits that follow from it
notes.ctx: 卡内基怕遗产削弱的，正是子孙的这股劲儿。
notes.ex1: What the partners valued was less her CV than her work ethic. 合伙人看重的与其说是她的履历，不如说是她的拼劲。
notes.ex2: Nobody doubted his talent; plenty doubted his work ethic. 没人怀疑他的天赋，怀疑他勤奋程度的人倒不少。

notes.en: bequeath means to leave property or money to someone by means of a will
notes.ctx: 指挪威研究里“被遗赠 30 万克朗及以上”的那批继承人；those bequeathed 是过去分词作后置定语。
notes.ex1: She bequeathed the entire archive to a university library she had never visited. 她把全部档案遗赠给了一所自己从没去过的大学图书馆。
notes.ex2: The bequest came with one condition: the collection must never be split up. 这笔遗赠附带一个条件：藏品永远不得拆分。

paragraphs.en_html: This makes investments in human capital more <mark class="voc">appealing</mark>. In the 1970s and 1980s Gary Becker and Nigel Tomes, another pair of economists, <mark class="voc">theorised</mark> that parents were <mark class="voc">better off</mark> investing in education and skills <mark class="voc">early on</mark>. For example, teaching a child to read is not hugely expensive, but opens up huge opportunities for future earnings. Investing in financial assets starts to <mark class="voc">make sense</mark> later, once those human-capital investments encounter <mark class="voc">diminishing returns</mark>. <mark class="voc">A wealth of</mark> <mark class="voc">empirical</mark> evidence has since <mark class="voc">backed up</mark> the theory.
paragraphs.zh: 这么一来，投资人力资本就显得更有吸引力了。上世纪七八十年代，加里·贝克尔和奈杰尔·汤姆斯这另一对经济学家就从理论上论证过：父母趁早把钱投在教育和技能上，更划算。举个例子，教孩子认字花不了几个钱，却能为他将来的收入打开巨大的空间。至于往金融资产上投钱，那是后面的事——等人力资本的投入开始遭遇边际收益递减，再投也不迟。此后几十年间，大量实证研究都为这套理论提供了支撑。

notes.en: appealing means attractive, interesting, or likely to win someone’s support
notes.zh: 有吸引力的，让人心动的
notes.ctx: 既然财富可能养废孩子，投资人力资本这条路就显得更划算。
notes.ex1: The offer was appealing right up until the lock-up clause appeared. 这个报价一直很诱人，直到锁定条款出现。
notes.ex2: The charity appealed for emergency funding within hours of the quake. 地震后几个小时内，这家慈善机构就发出了紧急募款呼吁。

notes.en: theorise means to put forward a formal theory or model to explain something
notes.zh: 从理论上提出，建模论证
notes.ctx: 贝克尔与汤姆斯在七八十年代提出的“先投教育、后投金融”的模型——用这个词而非 say，说明是有推演的。
notes.ex1: Researchers theorise that the collapse began decades before the first visible crack. 研究者推断，这场崩塌早在第一道可见裂缝出现之前几十年就已开始。
notes.ex2: It is easy to theorise about resilience and hard to build it. 谈论韧性很容易，造出韧性很难。

notes.en: to be better off means to be in a more favourable position, financially or otherwise
notes.ctx: 父母“早早投教育更划算”；第 9 段又用它比较钱放免税账户还是放父母的证券账户。
notes.ex1: Most households would be better off switching tariffs than haggling over the bill. 多数家庭与其跟账单较劲，不如换个资费套餐更划算。
notes.ex2: Ten years on, the bottom quintile is no better off in real terms. 十年过去，最低收入的那五分之一人群，按实际购买力算并没有变好。

notes.en: early on means at an early stage in a process or period, rather than merely at an early time
notes.ctx: 贝克尔理论的关键时点：教育和技能投入要趁早，不是等孩子大了再砸钱。
notes.ex1: We decided early on that we would not take outside money. 我们一开始就定了不拿外部投资。
notes.ex2: Problems that are caught early on cost a fraction of what they cost later. 早期发现的问题，成本只有后期的零头。

notes.en: make sense means to be reasonable, logical or financially sensible
notes.ctx: 金融资产投资“要到后面才开始变得划算”——作者在排先后顺序。
notes.ex1: Building a second plant only makes sense if demand holds through next year. 只有明年需求撑得住，建第二家工厂才划算。
notes.ex2: It took three readings to make sense of the footnotes. 那些脚注，读了三遍才看明白。

notes.en: diminishing returns means the point at which each additional unit of input produces a smaller gain than the one before
notes.ctx: 教孩子认字回报近乎无穷，第七个补习班的回报却很小；撞上这个拐点，才轮到金融资产。
notes.ex1: Past four engineers, the team hit diminishing returns almost immediately. 超过四个工程师之后，这个团队几乎立刻就撞上了边际收益递减。
notes.ex2: Advertising spend in that market has long since passed the point of diminishing returns. 那个市场的广告投放，早就过了边际收益递减的临界点。

notes.en: a wealth of means a large amount or a rich supply of something
notes.ctx: 此后几十年支持贝克尔理论的大量实证证据；在一篇讲财富的文章里用这个词，本身是个小双关。
notes.ex1: She brings a wealth of experience from two decades in emerging markets. 她带来了在新兴市场二十年积累的丰富经验。
notes.ex2: The archive contains a wealth of detail nobody has yet catalogued. 这批档案里有大量尚未编目的细节。

notes.en: empirical means based on observation, experiment or data rather than on theory alone
notes.zh: 实证的，基于数据和观察的
notes.ctx: 四十多年来验证贝克尔理论的那批研究；与前文 theorise 构成“理论—证据”的分工。
notes.ex1: The claim is plausible but still lacks empirical support. 这个说法看着合理，但仍然缺乏实证支持。
notes.ex2: Two decades of empirical work finally settled the argument. 二十年的实证研究，终于把这场争论了结了。

notes.en: back up means to provide evidence that supports a claim; also to make a copy of data, or to reverse a vehicle
notes.ctx: 大量实证证据“支撑了”贝克尔的理论。
notes.ex1: Every number in the deck is backed up by a source in the appendix. 这份材料里的每个数字，附录里都有出处。
notes.ex2: Back up the file before you touch the formatting. 动格式之前先把文件备份了。

paragraphs.en_html: Beyond basic skills, however, investing in human capital gets <mark class="voc">fraught</mark>. Such investments are <mark class="voc">sunk costs</mark> that cannot be <mark class="voc">liquidated</mark>. They are also <mark class="voc">infungible</mark>: <mark class="voc">tutoring</mark> in advanced maths is not the same as Chinese lessons. Children react differently (and <mark class="voc">unpredictably</mark>) to each. The extraordinarily long <mark class="voc">timeframes</mark> that make investing for babies attractive also raise uncertainty. Perhaps the skills that are valuable today will be <mark class="voc">obsolete</mark> in an AI future?
paragraphs.zh: 不过，一旦越过基础技能这条线，投资人力资本就开始变得棘手了。这类投入是沉没成本，收不回也变不了现。它们还彼此不可替换：补高阶数学，和上中文课，根本是两码事。而孩子对每一样的反应都不一样——还没法预测。更麻烦的是，正是那个让“给婴儿投资”显得诱人的超长时间跨度，同时也把不确定性一路推高。说不定今天还值钱的本事，到了AI主导的未来，早就作废了呢？

notes.en: fraught means filled with difficulties or tension; or, with “with”, loaded with something undesirable
notes.ctx: 一旦越过基础技能，人力资本投资就进入了“装得太满、随时要翻”的状态。
notes.ex1: Any attempt to reprice the contract now would be fraught with legal risk. 现在想给合同重新定价，法律风险极大。
notes.ex2: Negotiations resumed in a fraught atmosphere after the leak. 泄密之后，谈判在紧绷的气氛中重启。

notes.en: a sunk cost means money or effort already spent that cannot be recovered, and which therefore should not influence future decisions
notes.ctx: 花在孩子教育上的钱和时间，收不回也变不了现——这是人力资本与金融资本最本质的区别。
notes.ex1: The research spend is a sunk cost; the only question is what to do next. 那笔研发支出已经沉没了，现在唯一的问题是下一步怎么办。
notes.ex2: Four years in, they kept funding it out of pure sunk-cost fallacy. 投入四年之后，他们继续砸钱纯粹是沉没成本谬误在作祟。

notes.en: liquidate means to convert assets into cash; also, to close down a business and sell off what it owns
notes.ctx: 教育投入“没法变现”：你能卖掉股票，卖不掉孩子学了十年的钢琴。
notes.ex1: The fund had to liquidate its most liquid holdings first, which made things worse. 基金不得不先卖掉流动性最好的持仓，结果反而加剧了问题。
notes.ex2: Property is a fine asset and a terribly illiquid one. 房产是个不错的资产，也是个极度难变现的资产。

notes.en: infungible means not interchangeable with another item of the same kind, because each unit is distinct
notes.zh: 不可替代的，不能互换的
notes.ctx: 补高阶数学和上中文课不是一回事，而 100 块股票和 100 块债券却随时可以互换。
notes.ex1: Cash is perfectly fungible; a decade of someone’s childhood is not. 现金是完全可以互换的；一个人十年的童年不是。
notes.ex2: The whole premise of an NFT is that the asset is non-fungible. NFT 的全部前提就在于这项资产不可替代。

notes.en: tutoring means private teaching given to one student or a very small group
notes.ctx: 作者用它举例，说明人力资本的各项投入彼此不可替换。
notes.ex1: Private tutoring has quietly become one of the city’s largest service industries. 私人辅导悄悄成了这座城市最大的服务业之一。
notes.ex2: Two hours of tutoring a week lifted her grade more than the summer camp did. 每周两小时的辅导，对她成绩的帮助比那个夏令营大。

notes.en: unpredictably means in a way that cannot be foreseen or anticipated
notes.ctx: 括号里那个真正的杀招：孩子对每一项投入的反应不仅各不相同，而且根本算不出来。
notes.ex1: Supply chains behave unpredictably once a single node goes offline. 只要一个节点掉线，供应链的表现就变得无法预测。
notes.ex2: His one consistent trait was that he was completely unpredictable. 他唯一稳定的特点就是完全不可预测。

notes.en: a timeframe means the period of time within which something happens or is planned to happen
notes.ctx: 那个“异乎寻常漫长”的跨度，既是最大优势，又是最大不确定性来源；标题里的 knotty 在这句兑现。
notes.ex1: Nobody will commit to a timeframe until the permits come through. 在批文下来之前，没人肯给出时间表。
notes.ex2: Over a long enough timeframe, almost every competitive advantage erodes. 只要时间拉得够长，几乎所有的竞争优势都会被磨掉。

notes.en: obsolete means no longer in use or useful because something newer has replaced it
notes.ctx: 今天还值钱的技能，到了 AI 主导的未来可能已经没人需要；它不等于 old，是世界不要它了。
notes.ex1: Cheap sensors rendered an entire category of instruments obsolete within five years. 廉价传感器在五年内让整整一类仪器彻底过时。
notes.ex2: Planned obsolescence keeps the replacement cycle short and the margins healthy. 计划性淘汰让换代周期保持短促，利润率保持健康。

paragraphs.en_html: So what is a new parent to do? The most obvious financial options involve accepting free money. The $1,000 in a Trump account is a <mark class="voc">no-brainer</mark>. Even <mark class="voc">rabid</mark> anti-Trumpers would be mad not to take it. All parents should also accept similar <mark class="voc">grants</mark> from several American states. Those who expect to be <mark class="voc">on the hook for</mark> university tuition would be wise to <mark class="voc">take advantage of</mark> 529 accounts or similar <mark class="voc">vehicles</mark> as early as possible, so that compounding can work its magic to the full. Any money that children are likely eventually to inherit is better off in <mark class="voc">tax-friendly shelters</mark> than in their parents’ <mark class="voc">brokerage accounts</mark>.
paragraphs.zh: 那么新手父母究竟该怎么做？最明摆着的几个金融选项，其实都是在“白捡钱”。特朗普账户里那1000美元，想都不用想就该拿——哪怕你恨特朗普恨得牙痒痒，不去领这笔钱也只能说是傻。美国几个州还有类似的补助，所有家长也都该领。那些预计要自己承担大学学费的父母，明智的做法是尽早用上529账户或类似的工具，好让复利把魔力发挥到极致。至于那些孩子迟早会继承的钱，与其搁在父母自己的证券账户里年年交税，不如早点挪进免税的“庇护所”。

notes.en: a no-brainer means a decision so obvious that it requires no thought at all
notes.zh: 想都不用想的事，明摆着的选择
notes.ctx: 特朗普账户里白送的那 1000 美元——不拿才是傻。
notes.ex1: At that price, upgrading the insulation was a no-brainer. 那个价钱，换保温层这事想都不用想。
notes.ex2: Everyone called it a no-brainer right up to the moment it failed. 所有人都说这事闭眼都能做——直到它砸了。

notes.en: rabid means holding extreme opinions with an intensity that has passed beyond reason
notes.zh: 狂热的，偏执到不讲理的
notes.ctx: 指那些“恨特朗普恨到牙痒”的人——作者说他们不去领这笔钱也是傻。
notes.ex1: Even the company’s most rabid critics conceded the safety record had improved. 连公司最激烈的批评者也承认，安全记录确实改善了。
notes.ex2: Rabid speculation about the succession drowned out the actual results. 关于继任的疯狂猜测，把真正的财报数据都盖过去了。

notes.en: a grant means a sum of money given by a government or organisation for a specific purpose and not repayable
notes.ctx: 美国几个州提供的类似婴儿补助，与需要偿还的 loan 是两回事。
notes.ex1: The scheme pays a one-off grant rather than a loan, which changes the incentives entirely. 这个方案发的是一次性补助而不是贷款，激励机制完全不同。
notes.ex2: Don’t take a stable currency for granted; plenty of countries can’t. 别把稳定的货币当成理所当然，很多国家没有这个条件。

notes.en: to be on the hook for something means to be the one responsible for paying or dealing with it, with no way out
notes.ctx: 指那些预计要自掏腰包付大学学费的父母。
notes.ex1: If the subcontractor folds, the developer is on the hook for the whole bill. 如果分包商垮了，整笔账单都得开发商认。
notes.ex2: The settlement let both parties off the hook without either admitting anything. 那份和解协议让双方都脱了身，谁也没承认什么。

notes.en: take advantage of means to make good use of an opportunity; or, negatively, to exploit a person or their goodwill
notes.ctx: 尽早把 529 账户这类工具用起来，好让复利充分发挥。
notes.ex1: Exporters took full advantage of the weaker currency while it lasted. 汇率走弱期间，出口商把这个窗口用足了。
notes.ex2: He took advantage of her willingness to cover every shift. 她什么班都肯顶，他就一直占这个便宜。

notes.en: in finance, a vehicle means a structure or instrument used to hold and grow money
notes.ctx: 529 账户“或类似的工具”——钱坐上这辆车，被带到未来去。
notes.ex1: The trust is simply a vehicle; the real question is what sits inside it. 信托只是个载体，真正的问题是里面装了什么。
notes.ex2: They set up a special purpose vehicle to ring-fence the project’s debt. 他们设立了一个特殊目的实体，把项目债务隔离开来。

notes.en: a tax shelter means a legal arrangement that reduces or defers the tax owed on income or gains
notes.ctx: 孩子早晚要继承的钱，放进这里比留在父母的证券账户里年年交税更划算。
notes.ex1: Pension accounts are the most boring and most effective tax shelter most people will ever use. 养老金账户是多数人这辈子用得上的、最无聊也最有效的避税工具。
notes.ex2: Regulators spent a decade closing shelters that had been perfectly legal. 监管机构花了十年时间，关掉了那些曾经完全合法的避税安排。

notes.en: a brokerage account means an account held with a securities firm through which an individual buys and sells investments
notes.ctx: 父母自己名下那个要年年为收益交税的普通炒股账户，是作者建议的反面。
notes.ex1: Anything that does not fit in a retirement account ends up in a taxable brokerage account. 退休账户装不下的，最后都进了应税的证券账户。
notes.ex2: Zero-commission brokerage accounts changed who trades and how often. 零佣金的券商账户，改变了谁在交易、交易得多频繁。

paragraphs.en_html: Investments can <mark class="voc">misfire</mark>: violin lessons may generate <mark class="voc">little more than</mark> <mark class="voc">screeching</mark> and even a <mark class="voc">modest</mark> trust fund could encourage laziness. But with a bit of luck, investing in a child’s future and <mark class="voc">on their behalf</mark> will <mark class="voc">pay off</mark> <mark class="voc">handsomely</mark>. Fortunate parents with the ability to do both should approach this like the rest of parenting: try different things and don’t <mark class="voc">agonise</mark> too much over your decisions.
paragraphs.zh: 投资也会哑火：小提琴课最后换来的，可能只是一片刺耳的噪音；哪怕只是一笔不大的信托，也可能把人养懒。但只要运气不算太差，投在孩子身上的，和替孩子打理的，最终都会有相当可观的回报。那些有余力两头兼顾的幸运父母，不妨把这件事当成育儿的其余部分一样来对待：多试试不同的路子，别为自己的决定纠结太久。

notes.en: misfire means to fail to produce the intended effect; of a gun, to fail to discharge when the trigger is pulled
notes.ctx: 钱花了、课报了、琴买了，孩子就是不喜欢——该做的都做了，它就是不灵。
notes.ex1: The rebrand misfired so badly that the old logo was back within a year. 这次品牌重塑砸得太彻底，不到一年旧标志就回来了。
notes.ex2: His opening joke misfired and the room stayed silent for a long three seconds. 他开场的笑话冷了场，房间里沉默了漫长的三秒。

notes.en: little more than means only, and disappointingly so — no better than the thing named
notes.ctx: 小提琴课产出的“也就是一片噪音罢了”，那个“罢了”正是这个短语的情绪。
notes.ex1: The committee’s report amounted to little more than a restatement of the problem. 委员会那份报告，也就是把问题重新说了一遍而已。
notes.ex2: What was billed as a strategy turned out to be little more than a slogan. 号称是战略的东西，结果只不过是一句口号。

notes.en: screech means to make a loud, harsh, high-pitched sound
notes.ctx: 初学小提琴的孩子拉出来的噪音；作者选小提琴，正因为它在初学阶段最难听。
notes.ex1: The van screeched to a halt two feet from the barrier. 那辆面包车在离护栏两英尺的地方急刹停住。
notes.ex2: For the first six months, the practice room produced nothing but screeching. 头六个月，琴房里出来的只有刺耳的噪音。

notes.en: besides meaning humble, modest means not large in size, amount or degree
notes.ctx: “哪怕只是一笔不大的信托”也可能把人养懒——呼应挪威那个并不算巨款的 4 万美元门槛。
notes.ex1: A modest increase in headcount would not have solved a structural problem. 小幅增加人手，解决不了一个结构性问题。
notes.ex2: He remained strikingly modest about a career most people would boast about. 对于一段多数人会拿来炫耀的职业生涯，他谦逊得出奇。

notes.en: on someone’s behalf means acting for them, in their interest or as their representative
notes.ctx: 全文的收束：invest in a child’s future 和 invest on their behalf 被一个 and 并在一起，答案是“两条路都走”。
notes.ex1: She signed the agreement on behalf of all three shareholders. 她代表三位股东签署了这份协议。
notes.ex2: The trustees invest on behalf of beneficiaries who may not be born yet. 受托人是在替一些可能还没出生的受益人做投资。

notes.en: pay off means to produce a worthwhile result after effort or investment; also, to repay a debt in full
notes.ctx: 只要运气不算太差，投在孩子身上的和替孩子打理的，最终都会有相当可观的回报。
notes.ex1: Five years of unglamorous process work finally paid off this quarter. 五年枯燥的流程工作，这个季度终于见到了回报。
notes.ex2: They paid off the loan early and lost the interest deduction doing it. 他们提前还清了贷款，代价是丢了利息抵扣。

notes.en: handsomely means generously or in a large and impressive amount
notes.ctx: 两条路都走的父母“会得到相当丰厚的回报”。
notes.ex1: Early backers of the company were handsomely rewarded when it listed. 公司上市时，早期投资人得到了丰厚的回报。
notes.ex2: The restoration cost a handsome sum and was worth every penny. 那次修复花了一大笔钱，而且每一分都值。

notes.en: agonise means to spend a long time worrying anxiously about a decision
notes.ctx: 全文最后一句建议：多试几条不同的路，别为自己的决定纠结太久。
notes.ex1: He agonised for three weeks over an offer he was always going to accept. 他为一份本来就一定会接受的offer，纠结了三个星期。
notes.ex2: The wait between the scan and the result was the most agonising part. 从做完扫描到出结果的那段等待，是最煎熬的。

proper.name: Trump account / 特朗普账户
proper.def:
特朗普税改法案中设立的儿童储蓄账户：为符合条件的美国新生儿提供 1000 美元政府启动资金，资金锁定至 18 岁、只投低成本美股宽基指数基金，期间税款递延，满 18 岁后按传统个人退休账户（IRA）规则处理。法律已生效，账户尚未全面运作，首批政府出资预计 2026 年 7 月之后到位。
本文中的意思：作者列举的美国金融选项之一，也是第 9 段“白给的钱先拿”这条建议的具体对象。

proper.name: 529 account / 529 账户
proper.def:
美国的教育专项储蓄账户，名字来自《国内税收法典》第 529 条。税收优惠比特朗普账户更大，但资金只能用于法定的教育支出。
本文中的意思：作者用它和特朗普账户做对比，说明“优惠更大、限制也更多”这组取舍；第 9 段建议预计要付大学学费的父母尽早开户。

proper.name: Junior ISA / 英国少年个人储蓄账户
proper.def:
全称 Junior Individual Savings Account，英国面向未成年人的免税储蓄投资账户，每年有法定缴存上限（文中为 9000 英镑）。
本文中的意思：作者用来收束第 4 段的“税收优惠阶梯”——三种账户里税上最划算的一档。

proper.name: mutual fund / index tracker 共同基金与指数基金
proper.def:
共同基金是把众多投资者的钱集中起来、由基金经理运作的集合投资工具，多为主动管理；指数基金则被动复制某个市场指数的成分与权重，费率通常低得多。
本文中的意思：特朗普账户里那 1000 美元被允许投向的两类产品，对应“钱放进去之后具体怎么增值”这一步。

proper.name: UBS Global Investment Returns Yearbook / 瑞银《全球投资回报年鉴》
proper.def:
瑞银联合剑桥大学 Elroy Dimson、伦敦商学院 Paul Marsh 与 Mike Staunton 编制的年度报告，追溯 1900 年以来全球数十个市场的长期真实回报。
本文中的意思：第 2 段括号里“过去 125 年全球股市平均”那个 5.2% 的实际年化回报，正出自该年鉴；同一报告显示，1900 年投入美股的 1 美元到 2024 年底名义上增长到十万七千多美元。

proper.name: Ian Ayres & Barry Nalebuff / 伊恩·艾尔斯与巴里·奈尔伯夫
proper.def:
两位均为耶鲁大学教授——Ayres 身兼经济学家与法学教授，在耶鲁法学院与管理学院任职；Nalebuff 为耶鲁管理学院经济学与管理学讲席教授。两人 2010 年合著《Lifecycle Investing》，主张年轻人在二三十岁时用约 2:1 的杠杆持有股票，以实现“跨时间的分散”。该观点最早发表于《福布斯》时曾引来大量仇恨邮件；他们回溯 1871 年以来的股市数据，称这一策略的最终退休财富比传统生命周期基金高出约 90%。
本文中的意思：作者借他们的结论论证“时间越长越该担险”，再顺势推到婴儿身上——这套逻辑对二十来岁的人成立，对期限再长二三十年的婴儿就更成立。

proper.name: Andrew Carnegie / 安德鲁·卡内基（1835–1919）
proper.def:
苏格兰裔美国实业家，卡内基钢铁公司创始人，19 世纪美国钢铁业的主导者，也是现代慈善事业的奠基人物。1889 年在《北美评论》发表《财富》一文（后世通称《财富的福音》），公开追问“人为什么要给孩子留下巨额财富”，并认为让孩子背上这样一笔财富通常并非好事；他还直言，驱使富人留下巨额遗产的往往不是为孩子着想，而是家族的虚荣心。名言包括“我宁愿留给儿子一个诅咒，也不愿留给他万能的美元”。他后半生大规模散财，最著名的是在全球资助兴建数以千计的公共图书馆。
本文中的意思：作者用他作为“怕钱养废后代”这一担忧的历史原型，领出下文的挪威实证研究。

proper.name: the Carnegie effect / 卡内基效应
proper.def:
经济学中的正式术语，指“继承来的财富会削弱继承人的劳动积极性”这一现象，在关于代际财富转移是否应该征税的讨论中位置关键。
本文中的意思：文中那项挪威研究考察的正是这个效应——卡内基与挪威数据并非两件不相干的事，而是同一条线索的两端。

proper.name: the Norwegian inheritance study / 挪威遗产研究
proper.def:
挪威统计局研究者（Bø、Halvorsen、Thoresen）基于覆盖全挪威人口的行政数据库所做的研究，后发表于《Journal of Human Resources》。结论是：获得大额遗产者在此后六年内劳动供给显著下降，幅度在 7% 至 10% 之间，且效应随遗产金额、继承人年龄、是否享有其他转移支付、家族中是否出现新继承人而明显不同。
本文中的意思：为卡内基一百多年前的直觉提供了硬数据支撑。需要注意两点：7%–10% 相当于每周少工作约四小时，是“松了一点”而非“不工作了”；且挪威是高福利、工时本就较短的社会，结论不宜直接外推。

proper.name: NKr / 挪威克朗
proper.def:
挪威的法定货币，符号常写作 NKr 或 NOK（Norwegian krone）。
本文中的意思：文中的 30 万挪威克朗，作者已折算为“当时约合 4 万美元”，作为“大额遗产”的门槛值。

proper.name: Gary Becker / 加里·贝克尔（1930–2014）
proper.def:
美国经济学家，芝加哥大学教授，1992 年诺贝尔经济学奖得主，获奖理由是把微观经济分析的领域扩展到了人类行为与互动的广阔范围，包括非市场行为。他用“人是会算账的”这一假设去解释结婚、生育、犯罪、歧视、教育选择等传统上不属于经济学的议题；诺奖委员会认为人力资本是他最重要的贡献。他还有一个以名字著称的概念叫“坏小孩定理”（rotten kid theorem）。
本文中的意思：他与汤姆斯提出的“先投教育技能、等边际收益递减后再投金融资产”，是全文对那道取舍题给出的核心解法。

proper.name: Nigel Tomes / 奈杰尔·汤姆斯
proper.def:
经济学家，与贝克尔长期合作，两人在上世纪七八十年代合作的多篇论文（如 1976 年的“Child Endowments and the Quantity and Quality of Children”、1986 年的“Human Capital and the Rise and Fall of Families”）奠定了家庭内部人力资本投资与代际流动的分析框架。
本文中的意思：文中“另一对经济学家”里的第二位，与贝克尔共同提出第 7 段的核心理论。

sources_note: 资料核对：以上背景依据文章内容，并参考瑞银《全球投资回报年鉴》、贝克尔与汤姆斯 1979 年发表于《政治经济学杂志》的论文、挪威统计局遗产继承研究（Bø、Halvorsen、Thoresen，后刊于《Journal of Human Resources》）以及卡内基 1889 年《财富》一文等公开资料，数据截至 2026 年 10 月。

practice.intro: 请根据今天学习的外刊，把下面的中文句子翻译成英文。要求：尽量用上本文的核心表达，可以适当改变词形，但不要直接照抄原文。
items: 耐心、自律和节俭是投资者身上难得的好习惯，可这些美德在新生儿身上并不常见。
今天投进1000美元，按5.2%的实际年化回报计算（这是过去125年全球股市的平均水平），到孩子80岁那年，这笔钱将值58000美元。
花在孩子健康、教育和技能上的钱，回报率可能还要更高。
时间一拉长，波动就被熨平了，于是你反倒敢多担一些风险。
有些父母担心，设立一大笔信托基金，会把自己的后代变成游手好闲的废人。
正是那个让“给婴儿投资”显得诱人的超长时间跨度，同时也把不确定性一路推高。
practice.critical_en: If money can buy a child a better future, which is the better gift — a fund that quietly compounds for eighty years, or ten years of lessons, tutors and chances to fail?
practice.critical_zh: 如果钱能给孩子买一个更好的未来，那么哪一份礼物更好——一笔悄悄复利八十年的基金，还是十年的课程、补习和试错的机会？
practice.answer:
1. Patience, consistency and frugality are fine habits for an investor. They are not, however, common virtues among newborn babies.

2. $1,000 invested today with a real annual return of 5.2% (the average for global stocks over the past 125 years) would be worth $58,000 by the time the child is 80.

3. Spending on a child’s health, education and skills can yield even higher returns.

4. Long horizons smooth out volatility, allowing for more risk.

5. Some parents fear that creating a large trust fund will turn their offspring into layabouts.

6. The extraordinarily long timeframes that make investing for babies attractive also raise uncertainty.
